questions.question: Lead is ______ than any other metal.
questions.explanation: Comparative degree with 'than any other' takes comparative form 'heavier'.

questions.question: Mount Everest is the ______ peak in the world.
Iron is ______ than gold.
questions.explanation: Multi-syllable adjectives form comparative with 'more' -> 'more useful'.

questions.question: No other city in India is as ______ as Kolkata.
questions.explanation: Positive degree comparison using 'as... as' takes base positive adjective 'large'.

questions.question: He is the ______ of the two brothers.
questions.explanation: When comparing exactly two persons or things, the comparative degree with 'the' is used: 'the taller of the two'.

questions.question: She is senior ______ me by three years.
questions.explanation: Adjectives ending in '-ior' (senior, junior, superior, inferior, prior) take 'to', not 'than'.

questions.question: This cloth is superior ______ that one.
I prefer tea ______ coffee.
questions.explanation: The verb 'prefer' and adjective 'preferable' take preposition 'to', never 'than'.

questions.question: Milk is preferable ______ tea.
The higher you climb, the ______ it gets.
questions.explanation: Parallel increase/decrease takes double comparative: 'The + comparative... the + comparative' ('the colder').

questions.question: The more you study, the ______ marks you will score.
Shakespeare is greater than ______ poet in England.
questions.explanation: When comparing within the same class, 'any other' is required to exclude the subject itself.

questions.question: Gold is more precious than ______ metal.
questions.explanation: 'Any other metal' excludes gold from the rest of the metals.

questions.question: Very few countries are as ______ as China.
questions.explanation: 'Very few... as + positive adjective + as' takes base positive 'populous'.

questions.question: Of all the students, Rahul is the ______.
questions.explanation: Comparison among all students takes Superlative 'the most intelligent'.

questions.question: He is ______ than his brother.
questions.explanation: 'Older' is followed by 'than' for age comparison; 'elder' is never followed by 'than'.

questions.question: My ______ brother is a software engineer.
questions.explanation: 'Elder' is used attributively before a noun for members of the same family.

questions.question: Chennai is ______ from Delhi than Mumbai is.
questions.explanation: 'Farther' refers to physical geographical distance; 'further' means additional.

questions.question: For ______ information, contact the office.
Between Rahul and Rohit, the ______ is more hardworking.
questions.explanation: 'Latter' refers to the second of two persons/things mentioned.

questions.question: He arrived ______ than expected.
questions.explanation: 'Later' refers to time, while 'latter' refers to position.

questions.question: Have you heard the ______ news?
December is the ______ month of the year.
She is as ______ as her mother.
A deer runs ______ than a rabbit.
Which is the ______ planet in the solar system?
He is ______ wiser than clever.
questions.explanation: When comparing two qualities of the same person, use 'more + positive adjective', not '-er' ('more wise than clever').

questions.question: She is ______ beautiful than intelligent.
questions.explanation: Comparing two qualities in one person -> 'more beautiful than intelligent'.

questions.question: This is the ______ unique opportunity of his life.
questions.explanation: Adjectives expressing absolute states (unique, perfect, round, dead, complete) do not take comparative or superlative degrees; say 'a unique opportunity'.

questions.question: This is a ______ square.
questions.explanation: 'Square' and 'perfect' are absolute adjectives and do not take degrees.

questions.question: The pen is ______ than the sword.
questions.explanation: Famous proverb: 'The pen is mightier than the sword.'

questions.question: Honesty is the ______ policy.
questions.explanation: Proverb: 'Honesty is the best policy' (superlative of good).

questions.question: He is junior ______ all his colleagues.

Arjun is the ______ boy in the class.
A wise enemy is ______ than a foolish friend.
Blood is ______ than water.
He is the ______ person I have ever met.
Of the two routes, this is the ______.
She is getting ______ and ______ every day.
questions.explanation: Gradual increase takes repeated comparative: 'better and better'.

questions.question: It is becoming ______ and ______ to find affordable housing.
The deeper the well, the ______ the water.
Solomon was the ______ of all kings.
He is not as ______ as he pretends to be.
questions.explanation: Negative positive comparison 'not as... as' takes 'rich'.

Tokyo is ______ than most other cities.

Her ______ son is a pilot.
questions.explanation: Eldest among siblings in a family -> 'eldest'.

questions.question: This question is ______ than that one.
He is the ______ athlete in the tournament.
The climate of Ooty is ______ than that of Coimbatore.
questions.explanation: Comparison of climates -> 'cooler than that of'.

questions.question: The roads of Bengaluru are wider than ______ of Mysuru.
questions.explanation: Comparison of plural noun ('roads') requires 'those of'.

questions.question: The population of Mumbai is greater than ______ of Pune.
questions.explanation: Comparison of singular noun ('population') requires 'that of'.

questions.question: He is the ______ intelligent boy in our school.

questions.question: I spent ______ money than planned.

Jupiter is the ______ of all planets.
A plane travels ______ than a bullet train.
Nothing is as ______ as peace of mind.
He is ______ braver than prudent.
questions.explanation: Comparing two qualities in one person -> 'more braver' is incorrect, use 'more brave than prudent'.

questions.question: She is ______ younger than her husband.
questions.explanation: Comparative adjectives are modified by 'much' or 'far', not 'very' ('much younger').

questions.question: This book is ______ better than that one.
He is ______ happy with his new job.
questions.explanation: Positive adjectives are modified by 'very' ('very happy').

questions.question: Her condition is ______ worse today.
The dog is the ______ faithful of all animals.

The greater the demand, the ______ the price.

Ashoka was one of the ______ rulers of ancient India.
questions.explanation: 'one of the' is followed by a superlative adjective and plural noun ('greatest rulers').

questions.question: He is one of the ______ boys in the school.
Kerala is one of the ______ states in India.
He is ______ than I.
questions.explanation: In formal English, comparison between subjects takes nominative pronoun: 'stronger than I (am)'.

Change to Comparative: 'No other metal is as heavy as lead.'
options: Lead is heavier than any other metal.
Lead is more heavy than other metal.
Lead is heavier than all metal.
questions.explanation: 'No other metal is as heavy as lead' -> 'Lead is heavier than any other metal.'

questions.question: Change to Superlative: 'Lead is heavier than any other metal.'
options: Lead is the heaviest of all metals.
Lead is the more heavy metal.
Lead is heaviest metal than all.
questions.explanation: Superlative degree takes 'the heaviest of all metals'.

questions.question: Change to Positive: 'Mount Everest is the highest peak in the world.'
options: No other peak in the world is as high as Mount Everest.
Very few peaks are as high as Mount Everest.
Mount Everest is higher than any peak.
All peaks are not as high as Everest.
questions.explanation: Superlative 'the highest' transforms to positive with 'No other peak... is as high as...'

questions.question: Change to Positive: 'Shakespeare is greater than any other dramatist.'
options: No other dramatist is as great as Shakespeare.
Few dramatists are as great as Shakespeare.
Some dramatists are as great as Shakespeare.
questions.explanation: 'No other dramatist is as great as Shakespeare.'

questions.question: Change to Superlative: 'Very few poets in English are as great as Keats.'
options: Keats is one of the greatest poets in English.
Keats is the greatest poet in English.
Keats is greater than any poet.
Keats is greater than all poets.
questions.explanation: 'Very few... are as great as' transforms to 'one of the greatest'.

questions.question: Change to Comparative: 'Keats is one of the greatest poets in English.'
options: Keats is greater than most other poets in English.
Keats is greater than any other poet in English.
Keats is as great as other poets.
questions.explanation: 'One of the greatest' becomes 'greater than most other (or many other) poets'.

questions.question: Positive: 'A deer runs faster than a tiger.' (Equivalent meaning)
options: A tiger does not run as fast as a deer.
A tiger runs faster than a deer.
A deer does not run so fast as a tiger.
Both deer and tiger run fast.
questions.explanation: Comparative 'deer runs faster' transforms to negative positive 'tiger does not run as fast as deer'.

questions.question: Comparative: 'He is as wise as Solomon.' (Negative equivalent)
options: Solomon is not wiser than he.
He is not so wise as Solomon.
questions.explanation: 'He is as wise as Solomon' means 'Solomon is not wiser than he'.

questions.question: Comparative: 'I am not as tall as my brother.'
options: My brother is taller than I.
My brother is taller than me.
My brother is not taller than I.
I am taller than my brother.
questions.explanation: Negative positive becomes affirmative comparative: 'My brother is taller than I.'

questions.question: Superlative: 'Raju is the most intelligent boy in the class.'
options: No other boy in the class is as intelligent as Raju.
Very few boys in the class are as intelligent as Raju.
Raju is intelligent than any boy.
Raju is more intelligent than boys.
questions.explanation: 'the most intelligent' -> 'No other boy is as intelligent as...'

questions.question: Superlative: 'Ashoka was one of the greatest Indian kings.'
options: Very few Indian kings were as great as Ashoka.
No other Indian king was as great as Ashoka.
Ashoka was greater than any Indian king.
Ashoka was greatest of Indian kings.
questions.explanation: 'One of the greatest' in positive starts with 'Very few Indian kings were as great as...'
